problem.title: Two Red Tiles
problem.statement: A bag contains two red tiles and one blue tile. Two tiles are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both tiles are red?
hints: The first red draw leaves one red tile among two tiles.
Multiply the probability of the first red draw by the updated probability of the second red draw.

solutionSteps.title: First draw
solutionSteps.body: Two of the three tiles are red, so the first-draw probability is 2/3.

solutionSteps.title: Update the bag
solutionSteps.body: After a red tile is removed, one red and one blue tile remain, so the next red probability is 1/2.

solutionSteps.title: Follow the complete path
solutionSteps.body: Both draws must be red, so the path probability is (2/3)(1/2)=1/3.

validationMethods: independent unordered-pair enumeration: only {R1,R2} among {R1,R2}, {R1,B}, {R2,B} is favorable
notes: Recomputed answer: one of the three equally likely unordered pairs contains both red tiles, so the probability is 1/3.

problem.title: Two Gold Counters
problem.statement: A pouch contains 3 green counters and 2 gold counters. Two counters are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are gold?
hints: After one gold counter is removed, 4 counters remain.
The second numerator changes as well as the denominator.

solutionSteps.title: Choose the first gold
solutionSteps.body: The first counter is gold with probability 2/5.

solutionSteps.title: Use the new state
solutionSteps.body: Then one gold counter remains among four counters, giving probability 1/4.

notes: Recomputed answer: exactly one of the ten two-counter selections contains both gold counters.

problem.title: Two Even Cards
problem.statement: Cards numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4 are shuffled. Two cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both cards are even?
hints: After one even card is drawn, only one even card remains among three cards.

solutionSteps.title: First even card
solutionSteps.body: Two of four cards are even, so the first factor is 2/4.

solutionSteps.title: Second even card
solutionSteps.body: One even card remains among three cards, so the second factor is 1/3.

notes: Recomputed answer: only {2,4} among the six equally likely two-card sets is favorable.

problem.title: Exactly One Blue Tile
problem.statement: A bag contains 3 red tiles and 2 blue tiles. Two tiles are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that exactly one of the two tiles is blue?
hints: Exactly one blue can occur as blue-then-red or red-then-blue.
The two orders cannot happen on the same two-draw trial, so add their path probabilities.

solutionSteps.title: Combine the two orders
solutionSteps.body: The orders are disjoint, so the probability is 3/10+3/10=3/5.

notes: Recomputed answer: six of the ten equally likely two-tile sets contain one tile of each color.

problem.title: Same Color With Replacement
problem.statement: A bag contains 2 red tiles and 1 blue tile. A tile is drawn, its color is recorded, and the tile is replaced. After mixing, a second tile is drawn. What is the probability that the two tiles have the same color?
hints: Replacement restores the probabilities before the second draw.
Same color means red-red or blue-blue.

solutionSteps.title: Both red
solutionSteps.body: Replacement makes the red probability 2/3 on both draws, so P(RR)=4/9.

solutionSteps.title: Both blue
solutionSteps.body: The blue probability is 1/3 on both draws, so P(BB)=1/9.

validationMethods: independent enumeration of nine equally likely labeled draw pairs with five same-color pairs
notes: Recomputed answer: four red-red labeled pairs and one blue-blue pair out of nine give 5/9.

problem.title: Exactly Two Odd Cards
problem.statement: Cards numbered 1 through 6 are shuffled. Three cards are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that exactly two of the three cards are odd?
hints: Choose two of the three odd cards and one of the three even cards.
Compare those selections with all three-card selections from six cards.

solutionSteps.title: Count favorable sets
solutionSteps.body: Choose 2 of the 3 odd cards and 1 of the 3 even cards: C(3,2)C(3,1)=9.

solutionSteps.title: Count all sets
solutionSteps.body: There are C(6,3)=20 equally likely three-card sets.

validationMethods: independent ordered-path check: three placements of the even draw, each with probability (3/6)(2/5)(3/4)=3/20, totaling 9/20
notes: Recomputed answer: 9 favorable three-card sets among 20 equally likely sets.
